title: Kapisa
capsule: Kapisa was a regional polity centered on the fertile valley north of the Hindu Kush in present-day northeastern Afghanistan, controlling the strategic corridor between Kabul and Bactria. Under the Timurid and successor systems of the late fifteenth century it served as a contested sub-kingdom whose lords answered successively to Timurid Herat and then to the rising Arghunid and Mughal powers. By 1504 Babur took Kabul and absorbed the Kapisa region into his nascent domain, ending its function as an independent or semi-independent unit. The polity's attestation window of 1475–1507 reflects its existence as a named entity on the eve of Babur's consolidation.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial extent for this specific late-Timurid polity is poorly documented; boundaries are inferred from geographic references in Baburnama and secondary literature rather than contemporary cartography or administrative records.
